Date: 2026-04-22 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m

summary: Renewal and expansion check-in. Montclair is evaluating adding 2 reserved GPU capacity units and enabling Redwood in EU region to reduce latency for European customers. They are also discussing a 12-month contract extension in exchange for committed capacity discounts. Security and data residency (SOC2, KMS, VPC) are gating items. Redwood to send pricing amendment and run benchmarks next week.
topics: Additional region: deploy Redwood Dedicated to eu-west for lower latency and data residency
Contract extension: 12-month vs 24-month options and discounts
Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
Benchmarks: latency and cost per token, KV cache behavior
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check-in today to go over renewal and expansion asks from Montclair, a couple of agenda items. Marco will cover perf and benchmarks.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: thanks lena, yeah hi all, we're mostly looking at capacity and region stuff. our EU customers have been complaining about latency spikes, and we'd like to see options for adding eu region.
[00:30] Marco Diaz: cool, quick context — currently you're on Redwood Hosted plus one dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalents) with prefix caching on most workloads, right?
[00:40] Tom Reeves: yeah that's right. it's been stable but peaky, and around 08:00-12:00 UTC we see tail latency up. we think more dedicated capacity in eu-west plus local kv cache will help.
[00:55] Marco Diaz: ok, so options are (1) add 2 more dedicated GPUs in existing dedicated pool and enable cross-region routing, or (2) provision a separate small Dedicated pool in eu-west. Option 2 gives better locality but is a bit more expensive.
[01:12] Priya Patel: cost is a concern; procurement is asking for committed pricing if we extend the contract. what's the delta on price for adding region vs expanding existing?
[01:25] Lena Park: good question. ballpark, adding 2x reserved GPUs in same pool is about X% cheaper than a new regional pool because of pooling efficiency, but we can do a committed discount if you sign a 12 or 24 month extension. i'll send concrete numbers after the call.
[01:40] Aisha Khan: also, we need to keep data residency rules in EU for some customer data. can Redwood support VPC/private deployment for eu region?
[01:50] Marco Diaz: yes, we support Private deployments and VPC peering; for eu we can do a dedicated private control plane or a VPC option. small caveat: on-prem packaging vs managed VPC has slightly different onboarding time.
[02:05] Tom Reeves: onboarding time matters, we have Q3 go-live for a new product line. can you do the eu rollout in 3-4 weeks?
[02:15] Marco Diaz: 3-4 weeks is ambitious but possible if we pre-stage images and infra; if we need HSM/KMS integration there may be extra steps.
[02:30] Priya Patel: on KMS — we use AWS KMS and may want customer-managed keys. does Redwood integrate?
[02:36] Lena Park: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include the SOC2 appendix and key management docs.
[02:45] Aisha Khan: sweet. another point — we ran a small workload test and saw unusual token-cost spikes. is that KV cash behaviour or batching?
[02:58] Marco Diaz: likely both — if requests are small and not batched optimally you see higher per-token cost. we have batching configs and prefix/KV cache tuning; i'll propose a config and a benchmark script.
[03:12] Tom Reeves: please include headroom numbers — what throughput can 2 more GPUs give us, and how does latency change for 1k token prompts?
[03:22] Marco Diaz: rough estimates: adding 2x GPUs should increase sustained throughput by ~60-70% depending on model, and median latency for 1k tokens typically moves from 220ms to ~170ms in eu local deployment, but we'll run the benchmark to be precise.
[03:40] Lena Park: sounds good. procurement asked about termination and price protection; if you commit to 12 months we can lock pricing and offer a modest discount and some free burst credits. 24 months gets better rates.
[03:54] Aisha Khan: procurement prefers 12 months first. would that discount be tied to committed vGPU hours or token volume?
[04:05] Lena Park: typically committed GPU hours for Dedicated. we can model an equivalent token baseline if you need it.
[04:12] Priya Patel: security folks will want audit logs stored for 1 year, SSO (saml) and RBAC; does Redwood keep per-request logs for that retention?
[04:25] Marco Diaz: yes, we have request-level tracing and can configure log retention. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported; on Private deployments you can push logs to your SIEM.
[04:36] Tom Reeves: ok next, benchmark timing — we can open a window next Wednesday 14:00-18:00 UTC. is that workable for Redwood?
[04:45] Marco Diaz: yes, i'll plan for that window. i'll bring the benchmark scripts and we'll run the workload against a eu-west small pool that we pre-stage.
[04:55] Aisha Khan: perfect. one more thing — we mentioned Anthropic and Open AI as other vendors in the bake-off; procurement asked about feature parity around function calling and streaming.
[05:07] Lena Park: Redwood supports streaming and function/tool calling; we'll include docs and a short demo recording. some transcriptions in our notes say 'red wood dedicated' but that's just a rec.
[05:20] Priya Patel: haha, ok. also, is there an option to have a hybrid where some traffic stays in hosted and EU traffic goes to dedicated? we want to keep dev velocity.
[05:31] Marco Diaz: yes, smart routing can split by region, latency SLO, or path; you can keep dev on hosted and route prod EU traffic to dedicated.
[05:42] Tom Reeves: great. on SLAs — uptime and latency SLOs are important for us. What does Redwood commit to on Dedicated?
[05:50] Lena Park: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets and latency tiers; we'll include the SLA document as part of the pack.
[05:58] Aisha Khan: cool. any blockers from our side? procurement will need pricing and a sample amendment; security wants SOC2 + KMS guide; engineering wants benchmark script.
[06:10] Lena Park: action items noted. i'll send the pricing + amendment and SOC2 appendix. Marco will share the scripts and coordinate the run.
[06:20] Priya Patel: we'll confirm traffic numbers and procurement timeline by Friday.
[06:26] Lena Park: perfect — recap: Redwood to provide pricing for 2x GPUs and EU region, SOC2 docs, benchmark script; Montclair to confirm timeline and internal sign-off.
[06:35] Tom Reeves: thanks all. meeting adjourned.
[06:40] [call ends]
